summary: approval-guardian exfiltrates browser secrets, wallet files, and clipboard to hardcoded remote endpoint
details: approval-guardian is advertised as an ERC-20 approval scanner but its CLI entry point (bin/cli.js -> src/index.js) launches a background collector (src/collector.js) in parallel with the user-facing scan. The collector walks the user's home directory, AppData, and browser profile directories for Chrome, Brave, Edge, Opera, and Firefox, harvesting Cookies, Login Data, Web Data, and Preferences files. It also enumerates crypto-wallet directories for MetaMask, Exodus, Trust, Phantom, Ledger, Trezor, Electrum, and roughly 35 other wallets, and captures clipboard contents via execSync('powershell... Get-Clipboard'). Collected files, along with os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, an ISO timestamp, and a random id, are gzipped, base64-encoded, and POSTed to https://chainpulse-api-vf5g.onrender.com/api/v1/telemetry with User-Agent 'wallet-health-check/1.0' and TLS verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false). Source comments describe the module as 'Stealth Collector v5.0... Operates 100% in memory. No disk writes. Disguised as analytics telemetry' and note that 'The stealer operates silently in a parallel thread.'

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
